project.context: Hack am Rhein — Warm up with the city, 1–15 September 2026
project.core_idea: Plan a running loop through Basel that minimises measured air pollution exposure, where every number on the screen shows where it came from and every unmeasured street admits it.
project.one_line_pitch: Basel's trams measure the air as they cross the city. This plans your run around what they found.

product_thesis.problem: A runner breathes roughly ten times as much air per minute as a pedestrian, so route and timing matter more for runners than for anyone else — but nobody plans a run around air quality because the data is not in a usable shape.
product_thesis.solution: Join the mobile tram sensor readings to the walking network already in Basel Spatial Graph, score candidate loops by exposure, and let the runner adjust distance, pace and hour of day.
product_thesis.differentiator: Not the map and not the route. The join: measured readings, derived network structure, official statistics and a dynamic computation in one answer, each value carrying its own provenance class.
product_thesis.honesty_principle: Streets with no measurement render as unmeasured, never as clean. Absence is displayed, not interpolated away.
product_thesis.boundary: The system reports what the sensors measured on these streets. It does not claim a route is healthier, and it does not infer personal exposure.

viability_gate.status: UNRESOLVED — nothing below is committed until this passes

questions.question: Does the median reading differ enough between tram network segments to change a route choice, above sensor noise at the same location?
questions.fail_action: No route recommendation is possible. Fall back to a temporal-only or neighbourhood-level finding.

questions.question: Does the ranking of segments change between morning and evening, or is it one fixed pattern shifted up and down?
questions.fail_action: Drop the hour-of-day strip entirely and simplify the interface.

questions.question: What fraction of the walking network lies within 50m of any reading?
questions.fail_action: If coverage is very low, the unmeasured rendering becomes the primary finding rather than a caveat.

viability_gate.hypothesis_worth_testing: Ozone chemistry runs opposite to traffic pollution — NO from traffic scavenges ozone — so busy streets may read lower than parks on a sunny afternoon. If this holds in Basel's data, the counterintuitive result is the headline. Unverified.

computes: expected time from distance and pace
pace_control.why_it_matters: Slower means longer in the air. One line of arithmetic that no other running app does.

loop_generation.approach: Pick waypoints at radius, route between them, score each candidate by exposure. Return the best three.
loop_generation.honesty: These are candidates, not an optimum, and the interface says so.
loop_generation.rationale: True circuit optimisation with a distance target is the part most likely to consume the whole build.

provenance_model.principle: Ported directly from Basel Spatial Graph: the badge attaches to the value, never to the row or the response.

classes.measured: A tram sensor read this street segment. Carries dataset ID, retrieval date, reading count, and the reference-comparison error band.
classes.official: Retrieved from an authoritative published dataset, unmodified.
classes.derived: Persisted deterministic relationship — network structure, snapping, segment attribution. Carries the method.
classes.dynamic: Computed at request time from explicit parameters — the loop, the exposure total. Carries the parameter set.
classes.unmeasured: No reading exists for this segment. Rendered visibly. Never interpolated.

provenance_model.display_rule: A single loop must visibly show several classes side by side. That contrast is the argument.
provenance_model.visual_weight: Low. A footnote system, not decoration.

gpx_export.why: Every running app imports GPX — Strava, Garmin, Komoot, Apple Fitness. No OAuth, no API keys, no terms review.

extensions_block.purpose: Provenance travels with the file. Importers ignore what they do not understand; anyone opening it in a text editor sees where every number came from.

gpx_export.readme_note: State that a portable record format for this is the obvious next step. Credit for the idea without betting the entry on it.

success_criteria: A visitor drops a pin and gets a loop without reading instructions.
The visitor discovers one thing they did not expect about their own city.
Every number on the screen can be traced to a source in one interaction.
The GPX file opens in a real running app.
The repository is understandable to someone who has never heard of MCP or a graph.
Someone reading it says 'I did not know that about Basel', not 'nice map'.

risks.risk: The air data has no usable variation
risks.mitigation: Step 0 gate. Finding this out in an evening is a good outcome, not a wasted one.

risks.risk: Sensor coverage is too sparse for route choice
risks.mitigation: The unmeasured rendering becomes the finding rather than the caveat.

risks.risk: Scope creep back toward a running app
risks.mitigation: The explicitly_not_building list is the answer, re-read when tempted.

risks.risk: Loop generation consumes the whole build
risks.mitigation: Three candidates, not an optimum. Time-box it.

risks.risk: Reading exposure as a health claim
risks.mitigation: Framing stays at what the sensors measured on these streets.
